questions.q: Which device connects different networks and forwards packets using IP addresses?
questions.explain: A router works at Layer 3 and uses the destination IP address to forward packets between networks.

questions.q: Which OSI layer is responsible for logical (IP) addressing and routing?
questions.explain: Layer 3, the Network layer, handles IP addressing and routing.

questions.q: What is the PDU at the Data Link layer called?
questions.explain: Segment = Layer 4, Packet = Layer 3, Frame = Layer 2, Bits = Layer 1.

questions.q: How long is a MAC address?
questions.explain: A MAC address is 48 bits, written as 12 hexadecimal digits.

questions.q: Which of these is a private IPv4 address?
questions.explain: The private range is 172.16.0.0 to 172.31.255.255, so 172.32.1.1 is outside it.

questions.q: Which port does HTTPS use by default?
questions.explain: HTTPS uses 443. HTTP uses 80, SSH uses 22 and DNS uses 53.

questions.q: What is the correct order of PDUs when data moves down from the Application layer?
questions.explain: Transport makes a segment, Network makes a packet, Data Link makes a frame, and the Physical layer sends bits.

questions.q: What does a default gateway do for a device?
options: Receives traffic meant for other networks and forwards it
Connects Wi-Fi devices to the cable network
questions.explain: Traffic for any network other than the local one is sent to the default gateway, which is a router.
